articles.title: "The Secrecy Was Insane:" The Making of 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,' From Locked Safes to Original Cast's Return
articles.summary: Screenwriter Billy Ray, producer Nina Jacobson and director Francis Lawrence reveal how they adapted Suzanne Collins’ prequel before it was published, found their young Haymitch and brought back Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson.
articles.content:
Some stories refuse to stay on the page. The Hollywood Reporter’ s Beyond the Book column explores what happens when books make the leap to screen and beyond — unpacking what stayed, changed, how it was done and why it matters with the creatives who made it.

Before the odds could be in their favor, the creative team behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping had to survive a Games of their own, one played entirely in secret.

The rules were simple: one copy of the book, no internet and not a word to anyone. Related Stories Movies 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Hunts Down $21M in Box Office Previews Movies Jennifer Lawrence Thinks Her 'Hunger Games' Bow and Arrow Prop Was Stolen

When Hunger Games author Suzanne Collins called her trusted adapters, director Francis Lawrence , producer Nina Jacobson and original Hunger Games screenwriter Billy Ray , they were eager to read her new story. The catch: it wasn’t fully finished, and it hadn’t been announced to the public. That meant caution was essential. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Take Ray’s process for example. The screenwriter didn’t write his latest Hunger Games script on his own computer. Each day, he drove onto the Fox lot to Jacobson’s office and sat down in a small room with a safe that guarded Collins' story. An assistant opened the safe, took out a laptop that had never been connected to the internet and set it in front of him. He wrote all day, said “Done,” and the laptop went back into the safe.

“That’s how the script got written, which of course I had never done before,” Ray tells The Hollywood Reporter .

It was an unusual way to adapt a novel that almost no one outside that small circle knew existed, yet maintaining strict confidentiality was imperative given the phenomenon Collins’ franchise has become. The original four films — The Hunger Games , Catching Fire and Mockingjay Part 1 and 2 — grossed roughly $2.98 billion worldwide. Debuting with its first book in 2008, the dystopian saga following teenagers forced into fatal combat has grown into one of the most successful young adult publishing franchises in history. Across its five installments, the series has sold more than 100 million copies globally. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In 2020, Collins released her first prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , which chronicled the rise of the tyrant Coriolanus Snow. The film was adapted for feature film starring Tom Blyth and Rachel Zegler. Now with Sunrise on the Reaping , released on Nov. 20, Collins has returned to another familiar face: Haymitch Abernathy, the District 12 mentor Woody Harrelson played in the films.

The prequel revisits the world of Panem 24 years before the events of The Hunger Games , starting on the morning of the reaping of the 50th Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, when a younger Haymitch (portrayed by Joseph Zada ) competes. Sunrise on the Reaping opens on Haymitch’s 16th birthday, which coincides with the second Quarter Quell, where the traditional choice of one male and one female from a district has been doubled to two of each.

Though initially not among the four selected tributes for District 12, Haymitch is automatically volunteered as punishment for trying to protect his girlfriend Lenore (Whitney Peak) who reacts after one of the chosen boys tries to make a run for it and is shot by Capitol soldiers known as "Peacekeepers."

The Haymitch origin story answers a question fans have had since the first film: how the hopeful, mischievous kid became the bitter, drunken mentor to Jennifer Lawrence 's Katniss Everdeen and Josh Hutcherson 's Peeta Mellark that Harrelson played.

Ahead of the film’s release, Ray, Jacobson and director Francis Lawrence spoke with THR about working under an NDA bubble, finding their new Haymitch and reuniting franchise alums Harrelson, Lawrence and Hutcherson. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

When The Hunger Games was first adapted for the screen, screenwriter Ray and director Gary Ross launched what would grow into a global success. Since both Ray and Ross parted ways with the franchise following the initial installment, Ray's comeback to craft the backstory for a character he helped popularize represented a complete full-circle experience.

"Having launched that franchise, The Hunger Games has been such a blessing in my career," Ray tells THR . "I can't begin to enumerate all the ways it's been great for me."

"When the opportunity came to come back, I said yes before I read the book," he says of his return. "It was something I wanted to do. I wanted to work with Francis, and I wanted to be back under the hood with Suzanne and with Nina."

Ray has stayed close with Collins, who read an early draft of his debut novel, Burn the Water , which was released earlier this year. "It was as if we had spoken the day before," he says of reteaming with Collins and others for Sunrise on the Reaping . "There was just no falloff at all."

When Collins calls, producer Jacobson, director Lawrence and Ray answer, ready to find out what the author has created this time. But her first question is always the same: "Why don't you guys take a look and let me know if you think it's a movie?"

"This is always kind of hilarious… We read this one and said, 'Yeah, it's a movie, Suzanne,'" Lawrence says, laughing. Jacobson's answer was just as immediate: "My first response was, 'Hell yes.'" blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Collins' question is a sincere one, though, Lawrence explains. "She's very serious when she says it's OK to tell her it's not a movie. When you create anything, you're vulnerable, and when she hands something to us, it's usually not completely finished. She feels vulnerable about it and wants some reassurance that it really is worthy of being on the screen."

Getting that far took some doing. When the team read an early draft of The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , the world was in lockdown, so keeping it secret was easier, Lawrence says. Sunrise on the Reaping brought "a different kind of tension, because the book had not yet been published, so the secrecy and security around the project was pretty extreme," Ray says.

"For us, the secrecy was insane," Jacobson says. "We had one hard copy of the book. It had to be mailed or messengered from New York to L.A. in sections. First it lived at her [Collins'] agent's house and then eventually we got a safe for my office and it moved into the safe. There was one copy, and people could make an appointment if they needed to read it."

The secrecy extended to casting, too. "Even once we had our script, we couldn't release sides, or even use a scene from the book instead of sides, because if we read an actor, people would know what scenes and characters were in the book besides Haymitch," Jacobson says. "So we had the young actors do improvs, just so we could get acquainted with this generation of actors and start to collect knowledge about who they are." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Having to keep it locked down in this NDA bubble was exciting," she adds. "It was sort of stressful, and I was incredibly relieved when we could finally talk about it!"

"We knew Haymitch was going to be the trickiest person to cast, because we're anchored with him," Lawrence says.

Joseph Zada, who starred in Prime Video's We Were Liars and had filmed Netflix's East of Eden series, caught the attention of casting directors Debra Zane and Dylan Jury, who wanted Lawrence and Jacobson to meet him.

"He had sent in an improv tape. We had many, many people do improv tapes just to see who was out in the world, and his was pretty special," Lawrence recalls.

From there, the audition process became its own Hunger Games. "We really put him through the wringer in the audition process," the director admits. "We tested and tested to make sure he would be emotionally capable of going through everything he needed to go through, that he had the sense of mischief and irreverence Woody has, and that he could embody all those characteristics without feeling like he was doing an impression. That was the tricky thing. But he was definitely the guy."

"We needed to know he had the range to experience all of the loss in the movie, and to do it in different ways: sometimes shame, guilt or anger, or just complete loss and grief," Lawrence adds. "We needed somebody who could bring all of that." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Jacobson, the deciding quality was mischief. "You needed somebody who had mischief in them, and that's a surprisingly hard thing to find," she says. "There are some wonderful, likable actors who are very capable leading men, but who don't necessarily have that mischief in them, that troublemaker vibe. And yet at his young age, it can't be that dark, twisted kind of mischief-maker or trickster. It's a boyish quality."

Zada was someone who "had a hopeful, sunny disposition" and the mischief they wanted Haymitch to embody.

"When you first meet him in the original movies, you don't understand why he's so angry, drunken, broken and bitter. You assume, well, it can't be easy being a mentor for the poorest, most disadvantaged district out there," she continues. "What all of us wanted to see in this one, and what Joseph captured so beautifully, is that he was bright, funny, hopeful and very apolitical."

Zada's chemistry with Peak, cast as his love interest, Lenore Dove, sealed it. "You just felt it. You felt like this woman is the woman he loves. She's his best friend. She's the person who makes it all make sense for him," Jacobson says of their chemistry reads together.

"There's a quality about Woody, and we had to find someone who had that quality but wasn't going to get burdened by it," she says. "With all of our actors, we always said, 'We don't want impersonation. We want interpretation.'"

That philosophy extended well beyond Haymitch. From Kieran Culkin and Elle Fanning to Glenn Close, Jesse Plemons and Ralph Fiennes, Sunrise wasn't short on A-listers joining its younger, newer cast members that also included Mckenna Grace, Ben Wang, Molly McCann and Percy Daggs IV. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But joining an established franchise isn't always an immediate yes, Jacobson says. "There are definitely some people who just don't know the series that well, so it's about educating them about it, and making sure they know we're not looking for them to impersonate," she explains. "We want their interpretation of the character. If they don't know the series, oftentimes they have to go ask around a bit and talk to people in their lives."

Culkin and Fanning, who play Caesar Flickerman and Effie Trinket, have been candid about finding their own interpretations while respecting the characters Stanley Tucci and Elizabeth Banks originated.

"What we tell people who are new to it, and I really do believe this quite earnestly, is that it's one of the very few franchises where, for each of the renowned actors we cast, it is actually all about performance. It's never about prosthetics or visual effects," Jacobson says. (Well, almost never: "Of course we use those things sparingly here and there. Those are not Glenn's teeth," she notes.)

The appeal, she says, is the creative freedom that comes with everything being "rooted in performance." "You're going to be collaborating closely with Francis and the department heads on the creation, building and design of your character, and it's going to come down to meaty character work. You're very rarely against a green screen. You're almost always in a practical location with, hopefully, some other amazing actors in the scenes with you. I think these movies give each actor a real showcase of their talents, in a way that isn't always true in a lot of other franchises." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Jacobson recalls Sunrise on the Reaping being an "incredibly emotional" read. "I cried quite a few times, and then cried quite a lot at the end. I found it so fully moving and satisfying on so many levels."

But how do you adapt a book fans haven't been able to read yet? The creative team relied on being fans themselves.

"Nina and I consider ourselves fans, so there are a lot of things we fight to keep from the book, details we love ourselves," Lawrence says. "And Suzanne is obviously going to fight for certain things: making sure her themes, ideas, the spirit of the characters and their emotional arcs are there. So there's a good group of us there to protect what we think fans are going to love."

"The funny thing is, it's incredibly easy for me to know how fans will feel, because I'm the OG fan," Jacobson says. "I'm as obsessed with the books as any diehard fan, and so is Francis."

Still, some things had to go. "If I put everything that's in the book into the movie, the movie would be six hours long. You can't do that," Ray says.

Sunrise doubles the number of tributes competing in the Games, and the team knew they couldn't explore every one in depth. "Getting to know the tributes and understanding potential allies and enemies is one of the parts of these movies people really enjoy and are invested in. So figuring out how to balance the 48, and making sure we gave time and attention to the core characters whose stories are connected to Haymitch's journey, was a definite challenge," Jacobson says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The book is also told entirely from Haymitch's point of view, which posed its own challenge. "What we found even in the original movies with Katniss was that if she wasn't in a scene, the scene still needed to be about her in some way," Jacobson says. "But when you're only ever with that one person, there's important context and opportunities you might miss. So figuring out where to break with his point of view, when to show something he can't see or know, was a big decision in the adaptation process."

As for every other decision, the guiding principle was Collins.

"At the very beginning of the process, I asked Suzanne, 'What is this book about for you?'" Ray recalls. "She talked about the philosophy of the book: the philosophy of propaganda and implicit submission, the philosophy of Thomas Hobbes, David Hume and John Locke. And I said, 'Suzanne, what's the book about for you emotionally?' She said, 'It's about love and loss.' I said, 'Great, that's what I'm writing.' So anything that didn't stick to that had to go."

The Haymitch audiences meet in Sunrise is a far cry from the broken alcoholic of the original films. In Sunrise , audiences encounter a teen initially easygoing and unconcerned with politics. But his life transforms when he is forced into the 50th Hunger Games. Refusing to simply comply, he attempts to disrupt the Capitol's system and oppose President Snow, altering both his own destiny and the world around him. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid9' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Jacobson likens the young Haymitch to the "kind of guy who's probably not very serious about school and is just waiting for the end of the day to run down to the beach with his surfboard and his girlfriend, hang out and catch some waves." His attitude, as she sees it: "I can't do anything about this broken world that I live in, but I've got a girl I love and a family I love, and that's enough for me. Who am I? What difference would I make anyway?"

Jacobson sees Haymitch's arc as similar to Katniss', with a priority on family that grows to include their community and district. "Your circle of concern grows in each movie, and there's a cost to expanding that circle, a price to pay… But it's the things he hears and brings with him from Lenore Dove. He says the Capitol has all the power and always will, and she says that doesn't mean they always have, and it doesn't mean they always will. It's this notion that it's not a foregone conclusion that oppressive power structures can't be disrupted and ultimately destroyed."

The Haymitch of the film faces a dilemma: "What am I willing to give up for the people I care about? And what am I willing to give up to right these really profound wrongs and try to end the Games?"

"Seeing him get radicalized, and seeing him decide, even with all this loss, that the way to honor these people is to continue to fight: that was what was really important to me, and what I found really interesting and moving," Lawrence says.

"You see Haymitch in the other movies, and Woody does an amazing job portraying him, but people laugh with him," the director adds. "He's a drunk, and you just don't know the history. Now you follow this movie and see all that he went through, how long and hard he fought, all the years he had to escort tributes to the arena and watch them die. But he continued to fight and kept his promise to his girlfriend, his mother, his brother, to Maysilee (portrayed by Grace) and all of them." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid10' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For Ray, filling in that history was the point. "In that first movie, obviously Haymitch is just broken, with a real serious drinking problem and a lot of pain. This was the movie that explained all that, and it was great to do that sort of history retroactively, to say, 'This explains the behavior you've been seeing through all those movies,'" he says. "People know what happened, and the trick is saying, 'Here's the part you didn't know.' That's what we were going for here."

Collins doesn't write unless she has something to say, and themes have been the foundation of each Hunger Games book. With the original trilogy, she explored the consequences of war for teens. With the prequels, she continues to examine the state of the world.

"Look at the themes she's dealing with now and how relevant they are: there's a bit of a call to action, this idea of implicit submission, and diving into the use of propaganda to get people to submit. So there are fresh ideas that feel very relevant. There's meat on the bone," Lawrence says. "Take this idea of implicit submission. You can look at any government, whether it's authoritarian, fascist or one that calls itself democratic: as humans, we always agree to be ruled by the few. It's a bit of a call to action: don't be apathetic, stand up, voice your beliefs, and don't expect instant gratification, because change may take time. I feel that's very relevant now, but it's also timeless, because people are constantly fighting for their rights. You see it in Hungary, with the ousting of a regime, and in Brazil, where people actually make change. That's happening now, but it's also something that's been happening for thousands of years." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid11' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Ray says he approached both the original film and Sunrise as if they were "true stories."

"And they're getting closer and closer to being that, which is the bad news for us as a culture, and the great news for Suzanne Collins, because she has her finger on the pulse of something, and it does feel like a true story. If you think of it that way, you can write it as a screenwriter from a place of complete outrage," he says.

Haymitch's journey matters now even more given it's "a time when so many people feel like, 'What's the point of trying to make a difference?'" Jacobson says. "It's a story that is so emotional about how hard it is to try to make a difference. It's also about how what you set in motion today might not be realized for another generation, and how hard it is to continue to resist and to endure, knowing that the changes you hope for could take 25 years to accomplish."

Anyone who knows The Hunger Games knows the brutality of the story. "I think an audience that has bought into the concept that a government forces children to kill each other knows they're coming to see something dark," Ray says. "I don't think anybody is going to come away saying, 'Wow, I was expecting a musical. What the hell is this?'"

Even so, certain sequences in Sunrise had to be toned down to keep the film's PG-13 rating. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid12' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"There's a moment in the book where a character is holding the head of a child, and I thought, 'We're never going to be able to do that.' There were probably three moments in the book where I went, 'Come on, Suzanne, this is never going to happen.' And she understands that when we get into the process," Lawrence says.

The story's emotional darkness stayed intact, and Lawrence says it was "toughest" on Zada, who had to ride that roller coaster on set.

"Whenever we led up to certain days, whether it was a Lenore Dove scene or a Maysilee scene, it was always a little scary for him, because he knew he'd have to sit in those feelings for 10 or 12 hours, basically all day," he says.

The Games were filmed first, with the District 12 scenes shot later. "He was so happy to just be happy: going to work convinced he'd never get called in the reaping, having a nice scene in the meadow with Lenore Dove, being in the candy shop. He looked forward to those days," Lawrence says.

But the darker turns were never far off. "We also had to do things like shoot his and Lenore Dove's first scene one day and then, because we were in that location, jump to the end the very next day and do that whole scene (readers know the one.) That was tough on Joe. Even when he was happy to be happy, he knew what was coming tomorrow. That weighed on him more than it did on me," the director says.

Though the book and film follow a younger Haymitch, the book's epilogue, featuring Katniss, Peeta and an older Haymitch, was in the script from the start. "It was such a profound honor to get to write those characters again. It was just pure joy," Ray says. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid13' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I remember reading the epilogue in the manuscript and thinking, 'Wow, this is fantastic.' I found it really moving," Lawrence says of the trio's return in the book.

"The hope was always to bring them back," the director says of Harrelson, Hutcherson and Jennifer Lawrence. But because of the secrecy surrounding the book and the adaptation, "We didn't reach out to them until, I want to say, the day before the announcement. That's when I called the three of them."

While the team hoped for an immediate yes, they prepared in case scheduling conflicts or other circumstances kept the actors from returning. "We had already tasked ourselves with figuring out how to make the story as fulfilling as possible if it didn't happen," Lawrence says.

But there was no need to rethink the epilogue: the actors were "all very excited to return," he says. "Then it was really just a scheduling question: when can we get the three of them together and out to Germany?" the director says.

Francis Lawrence has stayed in touch with the cast, but working together again in the world of The Hunger Games made for an especially meaningful reunion. "I think it was a Wednesday night when they arrived, and I got a text from Jen that she and Josh were having a beer in the hotel bar. I was coming back from set, so I joined, then Nina joined, and our cinematographer, the still photographer, the sound mixer… It's the same group of people who have been making these movies for 16 years, so we had this great reunion of about 30 of us before costume fittings and all of that." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid14' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

With two prequel novels and films now out, the question is always whether there are more stories to tell in Panem. The creative team admits they're just as in the dark as everyone else.

"She only really writes when she has something to say, so I hope she has something she wants to write about in this world, because I would miss it a lot," Jacobson says.

Fans have been quick to name the characters they'd love to follow in their early years, with Finnick (portrayed by Sam Claflin) and Johanna (Jena Malone) at the top of the list, along with the first Hunger Games. After Sunrise , Jacobson's own fascination is Plutarch. "When I realized from this book that Plutarch has been playing a double agent for 25 years by the time you meet him in Catching Fire , that to me is pretty fascinating. How do you pull that off? How could you possibly live that close to such danger? And what compromises did you have to make? He is not a morally clean character at all, so I have a total fascination with him," she says.

If the prequels have proved anything, it's to never say never, a lesson Jacobson says the team learned early. "When we finished the original trilogy of books, we really thought we were done. We've never tried to make a movie without a book of hers. We only make her books. We never tried to develop anything that wasn't based on something she had given us as a book she was going to publish. articles.summary: A-1 Pictures The 2010s were filled with a lot of brief, but impactful anime series. A lot of modern notable hits got their start in the 2010s, but some of the most notable ones from the decade were anime that were only given 24 episodes or less. The 2010s were an era when even the more underground […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The 2010s were filled with a lot of brief, but impactful anime series. A lot of modern notable hits got their start in the 2010s, but some of the most notable ones from the decade were anime that were only given 24 episodes or less.

The 2010s were an era when even the more underground anime were being put on to streaming services. This resulted in a lot of smaller shows gaining interest and popularity by fans of the genre. It was an exploratory time where western anime fans were finally free to find other anime, and explore genres they may like. If you weren’t expanding your horizons during this time, then you may not have heard of some of the anime on this list.

The story of this anime and the themes it tackles still hit hard to this day. A group of childhood friends have grown apart after the death of one of their close friends, Meiko Honma, five years ago. Jinta Yadomi starts to be haunted by the ghost of his dead friend as she tries to figure out how to pass on into the afterlife. Yadomi begins to track down the old friend group so they can share their memories of Honma to determine what her last wish might have been.

The anime approaches the topic of torn friendships and childhood regret. It puts a cast of imperfect characters on display whose methods of coping feel realistic. The characters have all grown since five years ago, but they are still flawed and it shows. This anime shows the different ways in which people put on masks to hide their feelings. Each of the characters hides the trauma of losing their friend in different ways. As the series progresses, Yadomi (with Honma’s help) begins to bring them back together by getting to the root of why they fell apart in the first place. All the while they are still trying to help Honma pass on to the afterlife.

The story follows 17 year old Shinichi Izumi, whose hand is taken over by a powerful alien parasite. Shinichi learns that the parasite was actually after his brain, and that many other dangerous parasites also exist on earth. The parasites seek to inhabit a human host to then turn into horrifying flesh weapons and feed on other humans. Shinichi names his new parasite Migi, and together they work to protect other humans from falling victim to the parasites.

This anime has the perfect balance of horror and action throughout as Shinichi has to discover what the parasites are planning and confront them using his own powers. There are themes in the series like body and psychological horror, and also asks the question of what it means to be human as Shinichi finds his personality fading more the background as he and Migi grow stronger together.

The Disastrous Life of Saiki K was an iconic parody anime of the 2010s airing at an ideal time for the comedy it conveyed. The parody comedy in this one lent itself well to the environment of popular anime of the time. There are so many tropes that the anime pokes fun at in various genres. At the same time, there are plenty of fun jokes that work well on their own as well.

Kusuo Saiki is a near omniscient boy with many powers, including telepathy and telekinesis. The anime takes this grand concept and places Saiki in a normal high school where he works on solving problems without revealing himself. Every episode there is a new minor conflict that Saiki struggles to solve despite his powers. The set ups for the jokes, and the characters themselves, are hilarious. The comedy still holds up too as it's the sort of anime whose simple but fun comedy never ages.

Along with Steins;Gate , Erased was one of the most recognizable mystery anime of the 2010s, and it is still a gem to this day. There wasn’t really anything like it at the time, and its story had viewers of the anime on the edge of their seat all the way until the finale.

The story follows 29 year old Satoru Fujinuma, a part-time pizza delivery driver living in Chiba, Japan. When he finds his mother murdered in their home, he is sent back 18 years in the past to stop the events that led up to it. What follows is an episodic story that requires you to remember small details as both Satoru and the viewer try to discover what significance his childhood has in preventing his mother’s murder. The mystery plot of this 2010s anime is one of the most engaging that you can find to this day.

Along with Anohana , Your Lie in April was another big tearjerker anime of the 2010s. The anime tackles things like trauma and abuse while also having a gorgeous soundtrack and visuals. The story follows Kosei Arima, a former piano prodigy who has lost the will to play. He was once a well-known pianist who reached his skill level because of his abusive mother’s strict teaching. After his mother dies, he finds himself unable to even hear the sound of the piano when he plays it. He meets a young girl named Kaori Miyazono who slowly but surely begins to break down his walls and give him the courage to play for himself again.

The anime tackles surprisingly mature themes like trauma and grief. It shows the sorts of pressure that people striving to be the best are put under, and just how brutal the road to excellence can be. Kosei’s journey to begin playing again is very satisfying to watch, and the side characters in the series support the story in positive ways. There is a bit of romance in the anime, but the main draw is Kosei’s and Kaori’s difficult journeys as they both grapple with circumstances that try to prevent them from playing again.

What anime do you remember fondly from the 2010s? Are there lesser known 2010s hits that people should know of? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Emmy Rossum on Producing and Starring in 'Furious': "I Have Been 'Matrix'-Style Dodging Mega-Predators Since I Was Seven"
articles.summary: In front of an audience at the Newport Beach Film Festival, the actress reflects on her breakthrough in 'The Phantom of the Opera,' her quest for equal pay on 'Shameless' and her production company: "I like characters that are living in moral gray areas. That's something that I wasn't really able to do in the ingenue years."
articles.content:
"I have been Matrix -style dodging mega-predators since I was seven years old," actress-producer Emmy Rossum said during a recording of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Awards Chatter podcast at the recent Newport Beach Film Festival , where she was being honored with the fest's Outstanding Performance in Television Award for her work on Hulu's Furious . The drama series, which she also produced, tells a cat-and-mouse tale of a female FBI agent (Rossum) and a young female serial killer (Lola Petticrew), both PTSD-afflicted survivors of sexual abuse. "So," Rossum continued, "I firsthand understand the nuance and complexity of being a young person in situations like this and of being a powerful professional woman in situations like this." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Awards Chatter' Podcast Jessica Lange on Bringing 'Long Day's Journey Into Night' Back to the Big Screen, Returning to 'American Horror Story' and Retirement Rumors News Emmy Rossum Named RAINN Ambassador Amid New Partnership to Deepen Public Understanding of Sexual Violence and Survivorship (Exclusive)

Rossum, who was once described by the late Roger Ebert as “a phenomenal talent,” is only 40, but she has been doing outstanding work for nearly 30 years — in films like 2000s Songcatcher , 2003's Mystic River , 2004's The Phantom of the Opera and 2013's Beautiful Creatures ; TV limited series such as Angelyne (2022) and The Crowded Room (2023); and, of course, for 110 episodes over nine seasons on the TV series Shameless (2011-2019), several episodes of which she also directed.

As Rossum's time on Shameless came to an end, she launched a production company, Composition 8, which she now runs with her husband, Mr. Robot creator Sam Esmail, and a development executive, Sara Moskowitz. Their first project was Angelyne , in which Rossum played the eponymous Los Angeles billboard queen. They have since made several others. Rossum explains, "The throughline in things that I've been looking for is: I like characters that are living in moral gray areas. That's something that I wasn't really able to do in the ingenue years." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But obtaining choice material is not easy for a small company, even one run by a top young actress. "We have to be scrappy because we're not LuckyChap [Margot Robbie's company], and we're not Hello Sunshine [Reese Witherspoon's company]," she explains. "We're three people with this mandate of wanting to tell complicated stories about women that talk about something in the zeitgeist and culture and where we are now — and make really entertaining and fun stuff."

What led them to Furious , their most successful project yet? Rossum recounts, "I was like, 'OK, well, we're not going to land any of the hot books, so where do we go look? We have to look where other people are not looking. Let's look at all of the old movies that nobody's looking at. Like, they were good, so why aren't we looking there? There's got to be one that's got a good skeleton that we can uncover and figure it out.'"

That led them to Bob Rafelson's 1987 cult classic Black Widow , which starred Debra Winger and Theresa Russell as an FBI agent and serial killer, respectively. The material was nearly 40 years old, but still "feels kind of contemporary," she felt, noting eerie parallels with everything from the Jeffrey Epstein saga to the "Jane Doe" case at Cornell. So Composition 8 obtained the rights and set about putting it together. Rossum sold the show to Hulu via a text, recruited Liz Meriwether ( The Dropout ) to serve as showrunner and set about preparing to play cop-turned-FBI agent Alice Black, meeting with and shadowing law enforcement officials, consulting psychotherapists, adding considerable muscle to her small physique and more. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She reflects, "It's interesting to play a character who can hold so many complexities, who can be infinitely, bottomlessly vulnerable and terrified and afraid to be weak at the same time as being incredibly manipulative and physically and emotionally powerful and dogged and smart and underestimated. It was the role that haunted me the most, and it was a benefit that I came on so early, because I felt that I was working on the character for three years before we started shooting."

The first season of Furious , which rolled out in July and August, was described by The New York Times as “remarkable.” Rossum's part, meanwhile, was described by The Guardian as “the role of her life.” For it, she is now in serious contention for end-of-the-year honors — best actress in a drama series Critics Choice, Golden Globe and Actor Awards — and, next year, she might well become the first person with the name Emmy to, well, win one.

In the meantime, though, she's headed back to work: a second season of Furious was ordered just before its season one finale aired , and it starts shooting in January. She can't wait — but she also wants the industry to know that she's not only interested in acting in stuff that she also produces: "I'm still in the incoming-call business, so please hire me! I want great roles."

The Home Alone franchise is expanding. A sequel to the beloved holiday classic is in early development at Disney , The Hollywood Reporter has confirmed.

Macaulay Culkin , who portrayed Kevin McCallister in the original 1990 film and its 1992 sequel, Home Alone 2: Lost in New York , is expected to reprise his role. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg , the longtime comedy duo behind Superbad , Pineapple Express , Neighbors , Sausage Party and The Studio , are writing and producing the film under their Point Grey banner. The duo is also working with Culkin on his idea for the sequel. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business Disney and AWS Team Up to Create AI-Powered 'Star Wars' Robots Business Disney Beats Wall Street Expectations as Entertainment and Parks Power Latest Quarter

Chris Columbus directed the first two films , which grossed a combined $836.3 million worldwide. No director is attached at this early stage to the new installment.

He also shared his idea for a potential sequel, which would see Kevin as a widowed or divorced father raising a child of his own. "We're working on a bill for entertainment, which is motion picture, television — we're thinking about adding certain other elements, like for instance theaters," Trump said. But we're actively in negotiations on that, and that's going to be very bipartisan." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Trump has previously endorsed a production incentive, which would provide producers with a 20%-30% credit on domestic labor costs. The reference to theaters was new, however.

Cinema United, the trade group representing the theater industry, has been pushing for a bill to subsidize renovation of theaters. The SCREEN Act , introduced in July, would create a 30% tax credit, with a maximum award ranging from $250,000 to $500,000 per site.

Michael O'Leary, the president and CEO of Cinema United, hailed the bill upon its introduction, saying that towns across the country "will see a tangible and positive cultural and economic impact in their local communities."

Hollywood unions leaders have been in meetings this week with members of Congress to push for passage of the bill during the lame duck session, which ends in mid-December. Trump seemed taken with the idea of working on a bill with Sen. Adam Schiff, the California Democrat who led Trump's first impeachment in 2019.

articles.content:
A year after revealing a Miss Piggy movie in the works, Jennifer Lawrence has shared an update on the Muppet solo outing.

The Oscar-winning actress, who is developing the project with fellow producer Emma Stone and screenwriter Cole Escola , teased the status of the script in response to a fan question on Watch What Happens Live .

"I don't know! I always get in trouble for saying stuff," said Lawrence, before reluctantly sharing: "Um, we have a first draft!"

Last November, Lawrence first announced on Las Culturistas that she and 2x Oscar winner Stone were developing the movie with Tony-winning Oh, Mary! sensation Escola penning the script, marking the character's first solo outing since Jim Henson debuted her on The Muppet Show in 1976. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

When asked if the trio would appear in the film, Lawrence said, "I think so, we have to."

Shortly after, Lawrence recounted how they decided to give the "feminist icon" her own movie . Starting as a chorus pig on The Muppet Show in the mid-1970s, Miss Piggy gradually became a bigger part of the series, before becoming an icon in the late '70s and early '80s. Despite Kermit being the star, she's long hogged the spotlight from her froggy beau.

articles.title: Channing Tatum's Josephine Is Not An Easy Watch, But Here's Why I Think It's A Must-See Film
articles.summary: It's a movie that will always haunt me.
articles.content:
I was fortunate enough to see Josephine at the 62nd Chicago International Film Festival, and it’s quickly becoming one of my favorite films of the year. The film explores collective trauma, female rage, the justice system, and so much more.

Josephine works best with minimal knowledge of the plot. Therefore, I will try not to spoil any major storylines. At its core, the film portrays society and how it often scars and fails women and girls.

Many films touch upon difficult subjects. However, not many of them create an atmosphere as well as Josephine . You feel the weight of everything. The subject matter has been done a lot, and sometimes in ways that sensationalize an event to the point of losing the horror in it. Josephine treats the subject matter with care. We need films like this, especially given some of the recent headlines.

Many of the best courtroom dramas often end with a sense of justice being served. Whether Josephine ends with a positive result or a negative result, it doesn’t matter. It ends with a sense that nothing is completely resolved. That feels more realistic than movies with an impressive lawyer who saves the day.

articles.title: Jasmin Savoy Brown Bids Farewell to 'Yellowjackets' and Finds Her Way to 'Hadestown'
articles.summary: The 32-year-old actress reflects on the journey and how close the experience brought her to her co-stars: "They're more constant in my life than any romantic relationship I've had for the last seven years."
articles.content:
"They say it takes seven years to regenerate cells, and we've lived an entire life," Jasmin Savoy Brown laments. The 32-year-old actress is on the precipice of closing out one of the biggest chapters in her professional career with the final season of Paramount+/Showtime's Yellowjackets .

It's been seven years since the pilot of the show was shot, meaning she and the rest of her co-stars have spent much of their young lives making the series. On one hand, Brown is happy to see the show go out on a high note. At the same time, she's not sure what to do without seeing her co-stars as often. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Next Big Thing Gabby Windey Conquered Reality TV. Now She's Determined to Be Your New Favorite Actress TV 'Yellowjackets' Stars on Finally Escaping the Wilderness in Final Season: "Feels Like a Completely Different Show"

"We've had marriages and babies born and separations and moves, and a lot of us have lost people," Brown tells The Hollywood Reporter on a Zoom from New York. She's at home for a brief moment of rest before her nightly performance in Broadway's Hadestown .

"We have seen each other through full seasons of life," she says. "They're more constant than any romantic relationship I've had for the last seven years. It's going to be weird, but we're going to stay supporting each other forever."

For Brown, a Broadway debut is a lifelong dream come true. The actress and singer is currently starring as Eurydice in the musical Hadestown . Her dream of landing a Broadway role had previously made her afraid to give it a try. The production had asked Brown to audition two or three times over the last two years, but she'd turn them down each time. She didn't feel like she was ready. articles.title: 'Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow' Review: Oobah Butler Exposes Modern Life's Many Frauds in Nathan Fielder-esque HBO Comedy Doc
articles.summary: The British journalist/prankster explores the scams behind wine, music, dating apps, wellness products and more in this five-episode series.
articles.content:
With You Can See Everything putting Nathan Fielder on the minds of viewers who had never heard of Nathan for You or The Rehearsal , it's likely that HBO announced and scheduled new docu-comedy Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow in the hopes that people would compare series host/creator Oobah Butler to presumptive awards darling Fielder.

It's a borderline impossible comparison to avoid, particularly in the United States given that Butler's profile is far lower here than in the UK, where he likely finds it harder to perpetuate his brand of fact-based pranking on an unsuspecting audience. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Business 'GTA VI' Generates $3.79 Billion in "Day One" Sales Movies Teyana Taylor Sells Female-Driven Comedy to Warner Bros. (Exclusive) Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow The Bottom Line Entertaining, but too rushed to be deep or humane. Airdate: 11 p.m. Sunday, November 22 (HBO) Creator/Star: Oobah Butler Director: Daniel Lucchesi

I don't think that tying Butler and Fielder together quite captures the full Oobah Butler experience. His cheeky brand of muckraking, honed over years adjacent to actual journalism, has at least as much in common with Louis Theroux, Michael Moore or Mads Brügger, among other puckish truth-tellers. This doesn't mean that Butler does what he does better than Fielder does what he does, either — just that it isn't a guarantee that if you like one that you'll like the other, or if you hate one that you'll hate the other. Compatible! But different.

Even though it's airing on Sunday nights at 11, Oobah: Scams for a Better Tomorrow fits solidly into HBO's vaunted Friday late-night slot that The Rehearsa l and How To with John Wilson and Neighbors have filled with reality-based pseudo-mirth in the past. It's frequently eye-opening and occasionally funny, and it captures some important truths about the modern condition without ever feeling as revelatory or profound as it obviously thinks itself to be. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Butler, who has pursued his interest in scams and socially endorsed frauds through Vice exposés, a bestselling book and a variety of television documentaries, is (or was, given that some of these scams date back to COVID times) based in New York, where he can apparently fool people in various ambitious ways.

If you recall how Butler gamed the system back in 2017 to transform his garden shed into London's top-rated restaurant on TripAdvisor, you're prepared for the gambits that play out over the five episodes of Scams for a Better Tomorrow .

Each episode is a too-tightly-contained attempt at a comparable prank, starting with "Wellness," in which he attempts to create, market and sell a nonexistent product called "Lacrimé," a serum derived from the tears of children. In "Wine," he attempts to turn garbage wine from spoiled, smoky Napa Valley grapes into a commercial success. In "Dating Apps," he attempts to create, well, a dating app driven by AI. In "Music," he attempts to transform a 15-second musical hook into a viral social media phenomenon and then into a charting hit song. And, finally, in "Royalty," he attempts to discover what it would be like to be a royal by, well, becoming a royal.

I say "attempting," but at least to varying degrees, he succeeds in these missions, with the entertainment not so much coming from the thing he's doing as the way he's doing it.

Some of the facets of his scams — or counter-scams, I suppose — are predictable and surface-level. Like who ever would have guessed that if you get your friends and loved ones to spend a buck purchasing your dismal musical effort that you can make your way onto a fringe iTunes chart? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In other cases, Butler's strategies are far more nefarious and amusing, achieving their goals in unexpected or vaguely disturbing ways. He learns the workarounds and loopholes of wellness product claims and endorsements, attempts psychological manipulation to allow his subpar wine to win competitions, and even seeks out single princesses online looking for a potential mate.

And sometimes, there's a truly devious architecture to his process, like the way he gets a group of singles on his fake AI dating site to text each other while believing they're texting with a digital character.

The elaborately constructed pranks are the ones that feel the most like what Fielder did for several years on Nathan for You , the key difference being that despite his aura of detachment, Fielder cares about the people he's tricking. "Caring" can take the form of either contempt or actual empathy, which causes the viewer to either root for or against the people he's interacting with. That you can't guarantee from episode to episode whether, and how, you want Fielder to succeed becomes the uncomfortable friction of that series. The Rehearsal is much more dedicated to Fielder's subterfuge as an orchestrated operation, but it's the human touch that allows for emotional resonance.

Butler is, at least in the case of this series, not especially interested in "people." He's interested in the industries and institutions that we naïvely trust and all the ways their bugs can be exploited and manipulated. He wants us to understand that the wellness industry is a scam, that royalty is a scam, that contemporary, social media-driven music is a scam. If he has to run over ordinary and extraordinary people to make this point, whether it's the wine critic from The New York Times , the princess of Cambodia or those duped daters, he struggles to make us believe that he cares. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Perhaps to combat the notion that he's only invested in the process, to prove that he has a soul and an investment in the human side of his endeavor, Butler has several episodes built around conversations with attorneys, to whom he's explaining the full game. He talks the attorneys through what he's done with overt and unconvincing displays of concern, asking repeatedly if he's broken any laws and looking for reassurance that he isn't the villain here.

These conversations ultimately are there to answer the question of "How does he get away with this?" rather than "How does he sleep at night?" but Butler sometimes puts on a sad affect as if he has regrets.

Those alleged regrets get lost in a hurry, because at 30 minutes apiece, Scams for a Better Tomorrow simply doesn't have time. Even Oobah, who sometimes resembles a Chris Lilley sketch character minus the tendency toward blackface (or a John Early gag), is presented as the man pushing everything forward, not the hero or villain of the story. He's busy and the show is busy and episodes are often too rushed to be satisfying.

In this respect, Scams for a Better Tomorrow works almost in contrast to The Rehearsal , where Fielder's ability to build a bar set on a soundstage or mount a reality singing competition or tell Sully's life story with puppets is meant to appear almost magical in its sleight of hand. Butler is constantly showing his receipts by the handful. He zips through his most potent and possibly disturbing ideas — like the row of goggle-wearing children harvesting tears or the focus group he maybe goads into cannibalism with no time for reflection — which makes Scams for a Better Tomorrow far superior as a how-to manual than a piece of magic. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The "Dating Apps" episode might be the exception; it's the one that requires the most suspension of disbelief and in which Butler and the show's producers have to work the hardest to argue that even if they were duping innocent civilians, the effect was potentially, if accidentally, positive. I needed more episodic time and more visible empathy for the featured characters, and got neither. It isn't exactly clickbait, but it isn't long-form reporting either.

Scams for a Better Tomorrow is also a show that will probably work better when watched on a weekly basis than as a 2.5 hour binge, since the point is identical each time: Modern life is rigged and over-designed so that you don't notice how rigged it is. Kudos to Butler for making the point as clearly and as repeatedly as he does, but I kept waiting for more insight beyond that, more awareness of the cultural toll of living in a contrived world. Scams for a Better Tomorrow is content to prove its point, installment by installment, leaving any deeper critique to other series or other investigators.

With Circuit Breakers, we're looking to help elevate a new generation of rising comedic talent — comics with unique voices and original, well-honed material, who are not yet overly well known to either the industry or the general public.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A free Nintendo Switch Online promotion has been announced by Nintendo, letting Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 users snag three months of Nintendo Switch Online for free. Nintendo Switch Online at the monthly rate costs $4 a month, so this represents a savings of $12. This may not seem like much money, but right now, just on the Nintendo eShop, $12 gets you games like Slay the Spire , Persona 4 Golden , and LEGO Harry Potter Collection. Further, in an economy where a simple candy bar costs over $2, any bit of money that can be saved quickly adds up.

In addition to some Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake freebies , Nintendo Switch Online subscribers on both Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2 have until December 6th to get a 3-month free extension to their Nintendo Switch Online subscription when they purchase 12 months of a subscription. This 12 month subscription can be a brand new subscription as well as an extension to a pre-exisiting subscription itself.

Right now, the offer is limited to the UK . Whether it will come to the United States and other markets remains to be seen, but there's a decent chance it will. If not, there are ways to take advantage of the deal without actually being in the UK. Meanwhile, this offer is not only available with the standard tier, but the Expansion Pack tier as well. The Expansion Pack is not available monthly. It can only be purchased at the 12-month rate, which costs $50. Effectively it's a similar amount of savings compared to three months of the monthly subscription to the standard tier, which is marked up in price because it's not 12 months bundeled.

It's quite rare for Nintendo to runs promotions on Nintendo Switch Online, even during the holiday season. Nintendo Switch Online is already very cheap compared to PlayStation Plus and Xbox Game Pass, so there likely isn't much wiggle room to run these type of promotions. Whatever the reason why, the point is these type of NSO promotions don't happen very often, so those who can should take advantage of this one while it's live and an option.

Nintendo Switch Online is available via Nintendo Switch and Nintendo Switch 2. Right now, there is no official word or rumblings of any major changes coming to the subscription service, such as a price increase, but it does look like a new console platform may be coming to NSO soon .

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Although Solo Leveling has remained quiet for a while, with no official release dates announced for any of its projects, the franchise's live-action series has just taken a promising step closer to release. Netflix's live-action adaptation was first announced in July 2025, featuring a promising cast and the surprising decision to follow the K-Drama format. Filming for the series, however, began in May this year, and so far, there have been two updates from the leading actors offering insight into how production is unfolding. It is safe to say that the project is aiming for an ambitious release and could become a live-action adaptation that fans will remember.

However, no release date or window has been officially announced as of this writing. A report from Financial News , however, may have just confirmed a 2028 release window for the series. South Korean entertainment and production company CJ ENM recently celebrated the 10th anniversary of one of its programs, O'PEN, which supports aspiring screenwriters, songwriters, and, more recently, novelists. The announcement emerged from one of the program's writers, who is speculated to also be involved in writing Netflix's Solo Leveling live-action K-Drama. A closer look at the details makes the potential 2028 release window for this project all the more plausible.

Considering that filming for the live-action adaptation only began in May this year, and the latest update from actress Han So-hee, who plays Cha Hae-in , suggests that filming is still underway, there is still some time before production comes to an end. It is evident that a significant amount of effort will go into post-production to bring the series' fantastical elements to life. This will require the production company to dedicate a considerable amount of time, especially considering that the first season will consist of seven episodes. Since it is also following the K-Drama format, fans can expect longer episodes, with the first season potentially covering a major portion of the story, perhaps reaching the point covered by the anime's first two seasons.

This gives the anonymous report from Financial News much more credibility. With this, Solo Leveling has finally secured a potential release window for a visual project for the first time since the anime concluded in 2025. There is no doubt that the most ambitious upcoming project is the anime movie, Solo Leveling: Beyond the System , which will immediately follow the anime and precede its third season. However, there is still no confirmed release date for the movie, despite fans speculating that it could arrive next year.

That said, there is still a possibility that the anime movie could be the next project fans get to see, potentially arriving in late 2027 or early 2028. Either way, these promising updates suggest that after two years of silence in the visual and audio formats, the Solo Leveling franchise is preparing for major releases over the next couple of years, once again capturing the industry's attention and potentially breaking even more records upon its return.

articles.title: 5 Marvel Superheroes Whose Origin Stories Were Altered Beyond Recognition
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Marvel Comics has created some of the most iconic origin stories in the comic book industry. These origins often show heroes not only gaining incredible powers but also learning important life lessons. However, these origin stories have often been altered. Some of these alterations are as simple as updating the origin stories for the modern […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics has created some of the most iconic origin stories in the comic book industry. These origins often show heroes not only gaining incredible powers but also learning important life lessons. However, these origin stories have often been altered. Some of these alterations are as simple as updating the origin stories for the modern day. Other times, a superhero’s origin story is changed so dramatically that it’s practically unrecognizable from how they initially debuted. These changes have ranged from highly controversial to making these heroes even more complex and groundbreaking. When these changes happened, everything we thought we knew about our favorite Marvel heroes was revealed to be a lie.

Writers are always trying to leave their mark on Marvel’s biggest characters. One surefire way to do this is to add new layers to the heroes’ backstories.

The superhero twins Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver have been the subject of numerous messy retcons that toyed with their true parentage. Although their origin was kept secret for years, it was eventually revealed that they were the mutant children of Golden Age heroes Miss America and the Whizzer. Marvel writers almost immediately scrapped that origin, instead making the twins the illegitimate children of Magneto. This revelation made much more narrative sense and lent itself to plenty of great stories centered on familial drama. However, because the twins couldn’t be portrayed as mutants in the MCU , Marvel Comics changed their origin yet again. Instead of being Magneto's mutant children, Scarlet Witch and Quicksilver were made to be children kidnapped by the High Evolutionary and used in his mad experiments, which gave them powers. This retcon has since proven especially controversial, as it undoes a great deal of character development for Magneto, Scarlet Witch, and Quicksilver.

When he first debuted, Bruce Banner was portrayed as a brilliant yet average scientist who was exposed to gamma bomb radiation, turning him into a giant beast. Originally, the Jolly Green Giant was treated as a straightforward monster that was born from gamma radiation. However, later writers revealed that the Hulk was part of Bruce long before the gamma bomb. As it turned out, Bruce was abused by his father, David Banner, and developed a dissociative identity disorder. The Hulk was a split personality and the personification of Bruce’s suppressed rage. The radiation only gave the Hulk a physical form. Later, it would be revealed that Bruce and the Hulk were empowered not just by radiation, but by the all-powerful, malevolent One Below All that rests at the bottom of the multiverse. These retcons turned the Hulk from a classic monster into a creature drenched in both psychological and cosmic horror.

Professor X always tries to recruit more mutants into the X-Men, but there was one roster he made sure everyone would forget. The All-New, All-Different X-Men team, including heroes like Wolverine, Nightcrawler, and Storm, was first brought together by Professor X to save the original five X-Men, who had been trapped on the living island of Krakoa. However, it was later revealed that this new team was Professor X’s second attempt to rescue Krakoa. Beforehand, he had an entirely different X-Men team consisting of the mutants Kid Vulcan, Petra, Darwin, and Sway. The mission was a complete disaster and it was assumed that Krakoa and its monsters had killed every member of that team. To cover up the tragedy, Professor X mind-wiped everyone so no one would remember that the second X-Men team and its members ever existed. This action was made even worse by the fact that Kid Vulcan was Cyclops’s brother Gabriel. This reveal warped people’s perception of Professor X from a kind, selfless teacher to a master manipulator.

A huge part of Spider-Man’s appeal is how seemingly random his origin was. Peter Parker just happened to be in the right place at the right time when a radioactive spider bit him. However, later writers would introduce the idea that Peter was destined to become Spider-Man, and that it wasn’t even the radiation that gave him powers. This idea would be explored with the introduction of Ezekiel, who also had spider-based powers. He explained that he and Peter were both Spider-Totems, who are avatars of the Great Weaver. This mystical and cosmic entity spins the Web of Life that connects all worlds in the multiverse. Peter, along with nearly every other spider-based hero in existence, acts as a champion of the Great Weaver. Peter actively suppresses the full power that his status as a Spider-Totem provides so that he can retain his humanity. This retcon has been incredibly controversial, but it also led to the concept of the Spider-Verse .

At first glance, Thor’s origin as Odin's banished son seems simple. However, when Thor first appeared in Marvel Comics, he wasn’t even a god. Initially, Dr. Donald Blake was just a mortal man who found a stick inside a cave. When Donald grabbed it, he was transformed into Thor. The early comics made it clear that the “Thor” we saw was just Donald, given the powers and appearance of the God of Thunder. Over time, the line between Donald and Thor blurred over whether he was mortal or a god. These narrative inconsistencies culminated in Thor #159, four years after the characters’ debut, when Odin revealed the truth. It turned out that Odin had banished Thor to Earth, turning him into the mortal Donald Blake with no memory of his past. Not only would Thor abandon his mortal form and secret identity, but he and Donald would eventually become fully independent individuals.

articles.title: MrBeast Settles Lawsuit Against Ex-Dev Director Over Allegedly Swiped Files and Hidden Cameras
articles.summary: The former employee oversaw issues ranging from content production to fundraising to political advocacy.
articles.content:
MrBeast has settled a lawsuit from a former development director who allegedly stole internal company documents and installed hidden cameras at company offices.

Lawyers for MrBeast and the ex-employee, Leroy Nabors, told the court on Friday of a deal to resolve the case. Under the agreement, he'll submit to a forensic inspection of his devices and accounts to ensure that sensitive information has been removed and not been disclosed.

"Upon satisfactory completion of the Protocol, Beast will voluntarily dismiss this action," states the filing. The dismissal will be "without prejudice," meaning the lawsuit can be refiled.

Nabors started at the company in 2023 as an IT contractor before becoming head of the development team. Upon learning that he'd be fired, he allegedly swiped thousands of documents containing financial data and sensitive information regarding business transactions and company investors, plus blueprints detailing how the social media superstar develops megahit videos, among other intellectual property.

Nabors later wiped his laptop to cover his tracks, according to the complaint. When he was confronted by the company about the alleged theft, he said that the mass download was a routine "backup" he conducted in the "normal course of business" and refused to return the documents, the lawsuit said

In its investigation, MrBeast said it discovered multiple hidden cameras across its offices and a device attached to its servers containing an application that allows users to remotely access and control its network. The company suspects Labors to have installed them. Nabors' daughter contracted with MrBeast to manage its entire IT network and had access to the camera feeds, according to the complaint.

MrBeast brought claims for misappropriation of trade secrets and breach of contract, among others. It sought unspecified damages.

The lawsuit detailed some of the innerworkings of the media empire controlled by MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson. It described the company's development team as "deliberately flexible and multi-purpose, tackling issues ranging from content production to fundraising to political advocacy." The company maintains strict security protocols, limiting access to trade secrets to certain employees and storing such information in a separate network, according to the complaint. It routinely audits user access to critical shared folders and directs employees to regularly change their passwords, said the lawsuit, which noted that applications on company devices require user authentication and have a session timeout mechanism.

articles.title: Fired Home Alone Star Sad ‘Every Christmas’ He Has To ‘Put Up’ With More Stories About What Happened
articles.summary: It’s not such a merry Christmas.
articles.content:
Home Alone is one of the most beloved Christmas movies ever. Families watch and rewatch it every year around the holidays. For most, it’s a celebratory time, but for one actor, Daniel Roebuck, it’s bittersweet. Roebuck, if you didn’t know (and I didn’t), was the original actor cast in the role of one of the Wet Bandits, Marv, who was memorably played by Daniel Stern. Behind the scenes of Home Alone , Roebuck was fired by director Chris Columbus just four days into filming, and ever since, Christmas has meant he has to relive that tough moment.

Roebuck has had a busy career since, including big roles in movies like The Fugitive and Agent Cody Banks , but he never worked with Columbus again.

This all stemmed from a story Columbus recently recounted about filming Home Alone on The Wildmen Podcast , where the director explained that the studio would only pay for either Daniel Stern or Joe Pesci (who played Marv’s partner Harry), but not both. So Roebuck was cast and, according to Columbus, the first screen test with Roebuck and Pesci was “terrible.” Roebuck, however, disputes that version of the story, telling PageSix:

He added that he only worked with Pesci for one day. He also adds that, despite Columbus telling him they would work together (something Columbus also notes), that never happened, and they haven’t spoken since. Roebuck still doesn’t understand the reasoning behind his firing, but he doesn’t have any ill will towards Columbus, saying:

Ultimately, though, Roebuck didn’t star in the movie, and, at least according to Columbus, the director got the actor he wanted all along. It’s pretty hard to imagine the movie without Stern , but these events bring a little bit of a dark cloud over the casting. I guess in the end, Columbus did what he thought he had to do, but it’s easy to understand why Roebuck has mixed feelings about what many consider one of the best Christmas movies ever.
