Candle Media cofounder Kevin Mayer told an industry conference in Doha on Friday that he had not foreseen the impending contraction in demand for streaming content ahead of the company’s launch in 2021.

He was speaking six weeks after Candle Media hit the trade headlines for its sale of Reece Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine to Paris-based European content group Mediawan.

Candle Media originally acquired the company, behind Big Little Lies and The Morning Show , in 2021, as one of its first acquisitions for $900M. Mayer, who was talking on to the Qatar Film Committee’s Industry Days event in Doha via video-link from L.A., did not dwell on the sale.

“On the live action side, we gave it a really good shot with Hella Sunshine and other assets. It was okay, but they didn't work out to what we wanted, so we recently sold those,” he said.

Mayer did not go into details on why Hello Shine had not worked out for Candle Media, and there were no opportunities for questions from the floor.

His wide discussion, however, gave some insight into some of the challenges facing the company as well as triumphs led by its acquisition of Moonbug , the children’s media company behind shows such as CoComelon , Blippi and Little Ange l.

The former Disney exec, who oversaw the studio's 2019 acquisition of 20th Century Fox and also helped spearhead the creation of Disney+ alongside Bon Iger, said the idea for Candle Media had been sparked by the studios getting into streaming and taking their IP in-house.

This trend, he said, suggested that streamers without big inhouse production capacity would be on the hunt for high-quality content.

"We felt that the value of being independent in that sort of industry, that vertically integrated, would be increasing, and I think that is still true. Being independent and having that that ability to sell to any of the streaming services is great,” he said. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“We also thought content demand would continue to increase double digits a year… with increasing demand globally for high-quality content, like we were producing at Candle Media, which would provide us with the volume we needed to make all of our acquisitions work financially,” he continued.

“Starting in 2023, that didn't happen. In fact, the demand for streaming content actually contracted quite a bit, to about 35% below the peak of 2022. So, that part of our thesis was incorrect, unfortunately. We didn't see that contraction coming.”

The second premise on which the company was built, he said, was the belief that strong IP and stories could exist on multiple formats.

“They could exist on YouTube and on TikTok and on other platforms as short form entertainment… they could coexist in traditional film, on streaming and television and elsewhere,” he said. “Then they would open up other revenue platforms such as consumer products licensing, which we did a lot with Disney, games, music…”

Mayer pointed to children’s media company Moonbug, which Candle Media acquired in 2021, as having fulfilled that gaol thanks to shows like CoCocomelon, which was born on YouTube, and then repackaged for Netflix.

“We took those stories that came from YouTube, put them into one-hour compilations and licensed them to Netflix from 2021 to 2024. While CoComelon was the largest YouTube channel in the world, it was also the most popular Netflix show in the world. For three solid years, it was the number one streaming show and the number one YouTube show," he said.

He said the operation had not worked in the opposite direction for more traditional IP.

“We were hopeful that we could take traditional film and TV and cross it over into social media. That didn't work all that well. But what did work really well is taking social media storytelling and crossing it over to traditional. And you've seen Obsession and Backrooms … all this stuff is happening from that perspective.”

These questions surrounding Niko Bellic only grew louder when fans noticed that his character's voice actor, Michael Hollick, appeared in the cast list for GTA 6 . However, Hollick isn't mentioned in the credits of GTA 6 as portraying Bellic, but instead, a character known only as "The Hitman". Just who is The Hitman, though, and how does he play part in

WARNING: Spoilers for GTA 6 are mentioned from this point forward in this article. Read onward at your own discretion.

In short, yes, Niko Bellic does appear in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Niko appears relatively late in the main story of GTA 6 , as he ends up crossing paths with Jason and Lucia. He's aged quite a bit since we last saw him, with Niko even mentioning that he hasn't killed anyone since 2012. This suggests that he may have been able to briefly get away from his life of crime, which was his goal at the end of GTA 4 , but he ultimately got pulled back in.

As a whole, Niko doesn't end up being in GTA 6 very much. He only appears in two of the game's scenes in Chapter 5, the first of which is titled "Taking Liberties." In addition to his short screen time, Niko is joined by some of the music that was heard in GTA 4 . This makes his appearance all the more nostalgic for those who have been playing Grand Theft Auto for the better part of the past 20 years.

As for the reason behind Niko being referred to as "The Hitman" in the credits of Grand Theft Auto 6 , it's because that's his brief role in the game. When Niko first shows up, it's at the penthouse of Giorgio Gallo, who is one of the biggest crime lords in Vice City. Giorgio works in tandem with a European mafia to ship billions of dollars of drugs across the globe, but when he makes a mistake that results in said drugs being confiscated by the United States government, Niko arrives to take him out as a punishment for his error.

Ultimately, Niko agrees to give Giorgio one more chance to rectify his mistake. This results in him enlisting Lucia and Jason to help steal back the confiscated drugs. Once Lucia and Jason complete this mission, Niko shows up once again and is stunned that they were able to pull off such a difficult heist. He then mentions that he's now going to head back home, which is an obvious reference to his own residence within Liberty City.

Even though Niko never actually kills anyone in Grand Theft Auto 6 , it's clear that Rockstar chose to call him "The Hitman" in the game's credits just to preserve the surprise nature of his appearance. His brief cameo is one of the biggest moments in the entirety of GTA 6 and helps make the larger Grand Theft Auto saga feel a bit more cohesive.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is available now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

articles.summary: Fifty years ago, Sylvester Stallone’s movie about an underdog boxer toppled films like ‘Taxi Driver’ and ‘All the President’s Men’ at the Oscars.
articles.content:
If you want to know the behind-the-scenes story of how Sylvester Stallone got Rocky into theaters, check out I Play Rocky , opening nationwide Nov. 20, just one day shy of the original film's 50th anniversary. How Stallone typed up a screenplay in just a few days. How he waved away piles of money in order to star in the picture himself, despite the studio insisting on a bigger name (like, say, Burt Reynolds, Ryan O'Neal or Clint Eastwood). How shooting that beef-beating scene in the meat locker left Stallone with bloody fists and busted knuckles. What's not in the film, though, is what happened after Rocky 's Nov. 21, 1976, New York opening, which in some ways is just as incredible an underdog story. With no stars (except Burgess Meredith) and virtually no budget (even 50 years ago, a million dollars was a pittance in Hollywood), Rocky had no business becoming the biggest film of the year. But it ended up drawing blockbuster crowds — with audiences cheering as if ringside at a real boxing match — ultimately grossing $225 million worldwide, or about $1.3 billion in today's dollars.

Then there was round two, Oscar night. At the 49th Academy Awards , Rocky beat Network , Taxi Driver , All the President's Men and Bound for Glory for best picture, and also picked up a best director statuette for John G. Avildsen. articles.title: 'Best Pancakes in the County' Review: Nicolas Cage Goes Gonzo, Again, in a Dismal Action-Comedy That Fails to Match His Energy
articles.summary: A remote diner is the setting for Ken Sanzel's movie featuring a stand-off between corrupt FBI agents and a gang of criminals.
articles.content:
You have to admire Nicolas Cage ’s penchants for loyalty and consistency. His latest effort reunites him with director-screenwriter Ken Sanzel, with whom he previously collaborated on 2019’s Kill Chain , a film that few saw and even fewer liked. And it features the sort of gonzo trademark Cage performance for which he’s become both admired and ridiculed, in this case featuring a degree of misplaced commitment to the bit that definitely doesn’t pay off. The only saving grace of Best Pancakes in the County is the excellent recipe advice about the titular food that will definitely improve your breakfast gatherings. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Nicolas Cage on His Approach to Playing John Madden in New Biopic: "I'm Not an Impressionist" Movies 'Madden' Review: Nicolas Cage and Christian Bale Go for Broke in a Cartoonish Biopic From David O. Russell That's Strictly for Football Fanatics

This is the sort of movie that is routinely described as “Tarantinoesque” (a word that’s actually included in the Oxford English Dictionary, don’t you know) thanks to its convoluted plotting, eccentric characters, jokey dialogue, and propensity for Mexican standoffs. These movies are, with a few exceptions, invariably bad, but this one takes the pancake. Best Pancakes in the County The Bottom Line The worst movie in the multiplex. Release date : Friday, November 20 Cast : Nicolas Cage, Justin Long, Shelley Hennig, Ravi Patel, Brandon Mychal Smith, Lauren German, Kelly Greyson Director-screenwriter : Ken Sanzel 1 hour 38 minutes

Cage clearly participated in creating the look for his character, labeled in an onscreen graphic as “The Son of a Bitch.” Playing a ruthless criminal who doesn’t hesitate to shoot his partner while eating ice cream after a safe-cracking burglary goes awry, the actor wears hideous ‘70s-era clothes and a terrible perm wig, his make-up featuring extensive facial scarring and a porcine nose. He also employs a speaking style that sounds like he inhaled helium before every take.

After a prologue in which the S.O.B. steals a MacGuffin, excuse me, hard drive, from an FBI stash house, the bulk of the action takes place in a diner whose only employees are Cookie ( Justin Long , once again working hard in subpar material), the cook, and Dolly (Shelley Hennig), a waitress whose specialty is the breakfast item described in the title. The diner, surreptitiously owned by the S.O.B., is located precisely in the middle of nowhere. But that doesn’t prevent it from soon being visited by a large number of patrons — including the S.O.B.’s criminal associates led by Ryder ( Ravi Patel , seen to much better effect in the sitcom Animal Control ) and a cadre of corrupt FBI agents headed by tough-talking Agent Margot (Lauren German). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Much violent mayhem ensues, including many characters getting gunned down by a drone armed with an automatic weapon. None of it is remotely convincing, however, with the obviously low-budget film featuring the fakest looking CGI blood spatter effects this side of a ‘90s-era video game, and a final shootout shot so darkly you can’t make out what’s going on. Throughout it all the characters make jocular asides, with one series of exchanges relying on the notion that the phrase “hummus wrap” is inherently amusing. Needless to say, there are also plot twists, albeit ones you can see from a mile away, including the revelation that Cookie and Dolly aren’t exactly whom they appear to be.

Cage, absent from the proceedings for long stretches, gives it all and then some, to the point that you can feel his delight upon repeatedly uttering the phrase “I can’t find my thumb!” after a particularly gruesome incident. You half expect him to reprise his line “I’m Nicolas friggin’ Cage!” from The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent .

His efforts, as gonzo as they are, are all for naught, with the movie’s incoherent plotting, risible dialogue, and subpar filmmaking making it a torturous experience with nothing memorable about it other than its title. That the distributor doesn’t have much confidence in its prospects is evident from its simultaneous release in “select” theaters and availability on digital platforms.

articles.title: Jean Grey Has Finally Lost Everything, and It's a Perfect Reversal of Her Most Iconic X-Men Story

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Jean Grey's most famous story, without a doubt, is "The Dark Phoenix Saga." Her fall from grace, as the full might of her cosmic powers possessed her, led her to destroy an entire planet and, eventually, take her own life to keep the same thing from happening again. It's a tragic tale that still echoes throughout the X-Men comics today, especially since Jean has returned from the dead more often than not. In fact, she dies and returns so often that it's become something of a character trope, where Marvel must kill off Jean every so many years to meet a quota. Now, however, Jean isn't the character to die. Rather, she's the one left to pick up the pieces.

As of DNX #5, Cyclops seemingly died in his battle against the evil version of the Beast, the Chairman. Unbeknownst to everyone, Scott was actually saved or revived by the Chairman, but to the world, he's dead. Given their special psychic rapport, Jean knew immediately that her husband was gone, and now she's left to pick up the pieces of his death as she rockets towards Earth in fury and grief . This is one seriously compelling storyline, and one that harkens back to the most common criticisms of Jean's character.

Jean has died a lot in comics. Her first and most famous death was, of course, her noble sacrifice in "The Dark Phoenix Saga," and that was planned to be her final resting place, but this is comics, so nobody stays dead forever. Her return in X-Factor (1986) broke the seal on that, and after she died once more in Chris Claremont's legendary New X-Men (2001) run, the precedent had been set. Jean's death was always meant to serve as a major moment for the X-Men that would push them into a new era, just like her resurrections would. With that in mind, Marvel decided to repeatedly bring back Jean temporarily over the next decade and a half, only to kill her once again, calling back to these important deaths with less impact each time.

Jean hasn't died as many times as people meme about, but she certainly has passed from this realm more than the average character, and that has left its impact. Most notably, the character who faces the biggest challenges and changes when Jean dies is always Scott. He's repeatedly watched the love of his life give herself up for the greater good and vanish, leaving him to figure out how to keep moving forward . The majority of Scott's biggest pivots and developments come from moving on from Jean's deaths. Even his hard turn to mutant terrorism sparked from his brush with the Phoenix Force, for crying out loud.

This newest story, however, completely reverses this dynamic. For the first time, Jean has lost Scott, and now she has to live knowing that she might never see him again. He isn't bound to the cosmic embodiment of resurrection, nor do the X-Men have access to Krakoa's ability to cheat death anymore. Jean will have to face this grief and agony as a survivor, and that's incredibly dangerous. At the end of the day, Scott is a man who will always bury his emotions, and even when he loses control and cuts loose, at best he could bring down a mountain. Jean's power is built around control. She could throw the world out of alignment with a thought, and now she's facing the worst feeling she's ever had.

This new direction for Jean is definitely something her character has needed. The shift to her facing cosmic threats and traveling the universe, battling villains like Thanos, has been interesting, but it's also disconnected her from the relationships that people love. Namely, her marriage with Scott. But X-Men (2024) is about to change that, bringing Jean back to Earth without brushing aside her status as an undisputed universe-ending threat. This storyline has been set up since the very beginning, with Scott openly telling O.N.E. agents that, if anything happened to him, Jean would come back to Earth in a blaze of fury. He's been dropping these kinds of threats since issue #3, and said it explicitly in issue #10.

The first real step is stopping Jean from pulling a Dark Phoenix and destroying the Earth, which has been explicitly called out several times. Kid Omega is on the team for that exact purpose , according to Cyclops's own words from issue #10. Obviously, the team will talk her down before it gets to that, and Jean's new status quo will be learning how to live back on Earth without Scott. He was the one who kept the X-Men together. Without Xavier around to connect everyone through his dream, it fell to Scott, and now to Jean, to act in his stead. Scott was the X-Men's greatest leader, but Jean will have to be something else entirely: their heart.

She's far from the only one grieving Cyclops. Beast will take it especially hard, and the rest of the X-Men will be lost and directionless. Jean will have to remind them exactly why they fight the fight. She won't be giving speeches about mutually assured destruction or creating an endless number of contingency plans, but she will remind the X-Men of the humanity that their stories are all too often distant from. Jean's new direction will need to give her the chance to reconnect not just with the planet, but its people. The reason her deaths have always been such massive moments in X-history is that she represents the soul that inspires them to keep going when logic has failed. She'll have to learn how to be that once again in a world that has moved on without her, and how to pull everyone together when the beast inside of her wants to rip it all apart.

What do you think will be the main focus of Jean's arc going forward? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.summary: Sebastian Stan's Bucky Barnes will get new gear once again in the MCU this December. It's no surprise that Marvel's superheroes are getting an upgrade for Avengers: Doomsday. Not only is it tradition at this point for characters to have a new style of totally different costume for any new movie or show (gotta sell […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Sebastian Stan's Bucky Barnes will get new gear once again in the MCU this December . It's no surprise that Marvel's superheroes are getting an upgrade for Avengers: Doomsday . Not only is it tradition at this point for characters to have a new style of totally different costume for any new movie or show (gotta sell those toys somehow), but it's pretty seldom that they actually change all that much. We already know that some characters in Doomsday will be going to their comic book roots , but others are getting a fresh upgrade.

Having been a part of the MCU since Captain America: The First Avenger in 2011, Sebastian Stan's Bucky has had a variety of looks over that time. New international posters for Avengers: Doomsday have started to make the rounds online, including one for Stan's Winter Soldier that reveals a new Avengers costume for the character, that marks his seventh superhero suit in the MCU. Check it out for yourself below, with the image revealing that he has brighter armor this time around, one that seems pearlescent, like the quantum suits worn in Endgame .

It's worth noting that in the poster above, Bucky's costume looks like the one he's seen wearing in the post-credit scene of last year's Thunderbolts . That scene is confirmed to have been shot on the set of Avengers: Doomsday , meaning that the looks the characters are sporting there are the same costumes they'll seemingly have on across the film. Despite this, the image does make it look like the armor on Bucky's costume is brighter, so there's a chance it's a slight variant from what we've already seen.

Across the MCU, Bucky may have one of the most eclectic ranges of superhero costumes compared to his co-stars. The First Avenger had him in somewhat traditional army fatigues, while he became The Winter Soldier in the 2014 sequel. Civil War gave him a slight upgrade, but his appearances in Black Panther and Avengers: Infinity War gave his signature metal arm a new look entirely. From there, he changed looks once again in the Disney+ series The Falcon and the Winter Soldier , plus in Thunderbolts *, which saw him in at least two different superhero costumes. Revisit them yourself below.

With less than a month to go before Avengers: Doomsday is released in theaters, we can expect even more teases and confirmations about the film to start trickling out into the world. Though another full trailer is still expected to arrive eventually, so far fans are only getting updates piecemeal from across the internet.

Earlier this week, some fresh footage arrived from Marvel in a BTS video about Robert Downey Jr.'s MCU return. Though it was light on new details, it did include the hidden update that Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm is also getting a new superhero suit upgrade for Doomsday. Between that update and today's reveal of Bucky's duds, fans shouldn't be surprised if even more superheroes stop for a wardrobe change in between fights with the titular baddie.
